newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SOCCER-VISSEL KOBE SIGN AUSTRALIAN DEFENDER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VISSEL KOBE SIGN AUSTRALIAN DEFENDER.

text.p: Australian international defender Matthew Bingley said on Monday he had signed for Japanese J-League club Vissel Kobe.
The 25-year-old defender, who plays for Sydney national league club Marconi, said he had agreed to an 18-month deal and will leave for Japan on Friday.
Bingley was a member of Terry Venables' squad for the Oceania zone World Cup qualifying playoff against New Zealand on Sunday but remained on the bench for both matches.
"Playing overseas can only benefit my game and I'll get more international exposure in Japan than if I had stayed in Australia," Bingley said.
Kobe have strengthened their ranks after Danish international Michael Laudrup left last month to join Dutch giants Ajax.
Kobe's English manager Stuart Baxter said: "Matt is a young player of quality who is very athletic. He will give mobility to the midfield and is a huge investment for the future."
There were no details of any transfer fee involved.
Bingley will become the third Australian international playing in the J-League after striker Graham Arnold and defender Tony Popovic joined Hiroshima before the start of the season.
